title: Expressly conditional acceptance
summary: A condition requiring assent to new terms can prevent the writings from forming a § 2-207(1) contract.
notes: Dorton requires a clear indication that the offeree is unwilling to proceed without assurance of assent, and rejects mere “subject to” language on those forms. C. Itoh uses an explicit condition, but later performance forms a contract under subsection (3) without the unmatched arbitration term. Klocek finds an inadequate showing of conditional acceptance under the possible standards it considers. An effective formation-blocking condition does not by itself secure the desired substantive term.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 276–284. Open assigned page 276.
